papers.title: DiWALI: Diffusion Policy Learning in World Models via Latent Action Inference from Human and Robot Play
papers.abstract: Learning robot manipulation is constrained by the availability of action-labeled robot data, for both imitation and world models. Humans can demonstrate skills in seconds, but their demonstrations lack the required robot actions. We introduce DiWALI, a framework that learns and improves diffusion policies within a world model trained on human and robot play. DiWALI infers latent actions from consecutive frames using an inverse dynamics model, enabling world model training without action labels, and grounds them in robot commands through a decoder trained separately on robot play. Skill policies are trained over latent actions from action-free human demonstrations and improved with reinforcement learning in imagination. On the CALVIN benchmark, DiWALI policies trained solely from human demonstrations substantially outperform baselines trained with robot demonstrations. Incorporating human play into the world model training also yields stronger policies after fine-tuning than using the same amount of robot play alone. Experiments on a physical robot show that skills learned primarily from human demonstrations are further improved in imagination with a world model trained on human and robot play. Together, these results demonstrate that human experience can support both manipulation skill acquisition and subsequent policy improvement, reducing reliance on action-labeled robot data. Videos, dataset and code are available at https://diwali.cs.uni-freiburg.de.

papers.title: Action-Effect Memory Pretraining for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: We present AEM, an Action-Effect Memory pretraining framework for robot manipulation that learns compact temporal representations from vision-action history. Unlike prior robot representation pretraining methods that mainly focus on single-frame visual encoding, AEM targets the temporal nature of manipulation, where the current observation alone is often insufficient under partial observability. AEM models manipulation as an action-driven interaction process by interleaving visual and action features and applying masked modeling to recover missing content from incomplete histories, thereby learning action-conditioned state evolution. The Mamba-encoded output of the final vision token is used as a compact history representation, serving as the global context for decoding and downstream control. This design preserves a single-vector temporal bottleneck while keeping inference efficient. We evaluate AEM with Diffusion Policy and Flow Policy. AEM consistently improves manipulation performance in both simulation and real-world settings, outperforming baselines across clean scenes, cluttered and random scenes, and non-Markovian tasks. Ablation studies further show that history-aware pretraining surpasses single-frame pretraining and direct frame stacking, while reducing inference latency and computational cost.
papers.overview_sentence: We present AEM, an Action-Effect Memory pretraining framework for robot manipulation that learns compact temporal representations from vision-action history.

papers.title: Amplitude-Triggered Nonlinear Peak Filter Control for Disturbance Suppression of Gimbal Visual Servoing Systems
papers.abstract: This work develops an amplitude-triggered nonlinear peak filter control (NPFC) strategy to suppress highfrequency uncertain disturbances for inertially stabilized gimbal visual servoing on moving bases. Different from fixed-gain linear peak filtering, the proposed scheme utilizes a sigmoid function to construct an error-dependent variable gain: large control gain is activated automatically under large tracking error spikes to suppress abrupt vibration and backlash-induced disturbances, while near-zero gain is adopted at tiny errors to avoid sensor noise amplification. The devised NPFC is embedded as a plugin auxiliary module into the Youla-Kucera framework (NPFCYK) without modifying the original nominal controller, which effectively breaks the waterbed limitation of conventional linear feedback control and requires no prior disturbance frequency information or extra sensing hardware. Comparative experiments on a two-degree-of-freedom physical gimbal platform verify that the NPFC-YK scheme effectively suppresses high-frequency uncertain dynamics, significantly improving tracking accuracy and robustness in dynamic environments.

repos.description: Supervised Go2-W + PiPER mobile manipulation with RGB-D visual servoing and grasp planning.
repos.readme_excerpt: Z-Mobile-Manip Supervised mobile manipulation for a Unitree Go2-W EDU quadruped carrying an AgileX PiPER 6-DoF arm and a wrist-mounted Intel RealSense D435. What this is The near-field half of a three-repository stack: navigation drives the robot to a coarse standoff, and this system takes over from about a metre out and runs through to a completed grasp and return. An RTX 4090 workstation does perception, grasp synthesis, IK, planning and the operator UI; the robot's onboard NUC owns the D435, PiPER can0 , joint feedback and the Go2-W WebRTC base transport, joined over ROS_DOMAIN_ID=20 . Open-vocabulary text is grounded with YOLOE , tracked with EdgeTAM , and back-projected against Fast-FoundationStereo depth rather than the D435's raw stream. Grasps come from AnyGrasp with a local antipodal generator as fallback, are solved by a damped Gauss-Newton Pinocchio IK, and are checked against a capsule model of the platform's own fixtures ( configs/piper_collision_capsules.json — the only enforced representation of the chassis, NUC and Mid-360 LiDAR) plus an observed point cloud. repos.readme_excerpt: Whole-Body Humanoid MPC This repository contains a Whole-Body Nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) for humanoid loco-manipulation control. This approach enables to directly optimize through the full-order torque-level dynamics in realtime to generate a wide range of humanoid behaviors building up on an extended & updated version of ocs2 Interactive Velocity and Base Height Control via Joystick: It contains the following hardware platform agnostic MPC fromulations: Centroidal Dynamics MPC The centroidal MPC optimizes over the whole-body kinematics and the center off mass dynamics, with a choice to either use a single rigid body model or the full centroidal dynamics. This specific approach builds up on the centroidal model in ocs2 by generalizing costs and constraints to a 6 DoF contact among others. I am still working on documenting this. Until then a conscise explanation of the ocs2 centroidal model can be found here Sleiman et. al., A Unified MPC Framework for Whole-Body Dynamic Locomotion and Manipulation Whole-Body Dynamics MPC The whole-body dynamics MPC optimized over the contact forces and joint accelerations with the option to compute the joint torques for each step…
